## Verdict
- Answer: India's Smart Cities Mission (SCM, launched June 2015, 100 cities) spent most of its funds on area-based projects and command centres, and reached its formal end on 31 March 2025 (est.). Reported project completion is high; evidence of citywide outcomes is thin and contested.
- Decision: Treat the SCM as a source of reusable infrastructure (integrated command and control centres, ICCCs) and lessons. Do not treat it as proof of urban transformation when allocating funds or partnerships.
- Confidence: low - this brief uses memory only. No Prism calls were run, and all figures are estimates.
- What would change it: Audited, city-level outcome data (not output counts), or a Prism corpus pull that contradicts the estimates below.

## What the data shows
No live corpus was queried, so there are no volumes per corpus, lane or window. I cannot measure them here. All numbers are from memory, are labelled (est.), and should be checked before use.

- Scale: 100 cities were selected in rounds between 2016 and 2018 (est.). The mission was planned for 5 years from 2015-16 and extended to 31 March 2025 (est.).
- Projects: about 8,000 projects worth roughly ₹1.7 lakh crore were tendered or taken up, and roughly 90% or more were reported complete by the end (est.).
- Funding: The central government committed about ₹48,000 crore (est.), with matching state and urban local body funds. Most of the rest was meant to come from convergence, PPPs and municipal borrowing, and that share fell short (est.).
- Governance: Each city set up a special purpose vehicle (SPV). All 100 cities have operational ICCCs (est.).
- Established: area-based development (ABD) took the largest share of spending, and pan-city smart solutions took a smaller share (est.). Parliamentary standing committee reviews flagged slow fund utilisation and uneven delivery (est.).
- Contested: whether SPVs weakened elected municipal bodies, whether ABD benefited only small enclaves, and whether ICCC surveillance carries privacy risks. I cannot give a contested share; no sourced figure is available.

## Trend
Illustrative cumulative project-completion trend, from memory of MoHUA dashboard figures. Values are approximate (est.).

```prism-chart
{"id":"scm-completion","kind":"line","title":"Approximate share of SCM projects reported completed","unit":"percent of tendered projects (est.)","window":{"from":"2019-01-01","to":"2025-03-31"},"x":{"field":"year","type":"temporal"},"series":[{"name":"Completed share (est.)","source":"estimate","points":[["2019",20],["2020",30],["2021",45],["2022",60],["2023",75],["2024",85],["2025",92]]}],"caption":"Reported completion rose steeply, from about 20% to about 92% over six years (est.).","supports":"Reported project completion is high; evidence of citywide outcomes is thin and contested."}
```

The estimated change is about +72 percentage points from 2019 to 2025 (est.). This measures outputs reported by the ministry, not outcomes.

## Comparison
Baseline: budget actually released versus total approved, on a rupee scale (est.).

| Measure | Value (₹ crore) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Central funds committed | ~48,000 | (est.) |
| Total project value | ~170,000 | (est.) |
| Ratio, central share of total | ~0.28 | (est.) |

Central funds were therefore roughly a quarter to a third of project value, and the remainder came from states, ULBs, convergence and PPPs (est.). The exact split is not verified.

## Geography (optional)
I did not apply a geographic filter. From memory, the heaviest project volumes were in Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, and the Northeast and the union territories had smaller absolute volumes (est.). I cannot give sourced per-state numbers.

## Evidence
No documents were retrieved. I will not invent identifiers or verbatim quotes. The kinds of evidence to look for are:
- MoHUA SCM statement and dashboard (government, 2015-2025). It supports the output counts.
- Parliamentary Standing Committee on Housing and Urban Affairs reports. They support the utilisation and delivery critiques.
- Academic critiques of SPVs and ABD (urban studies journals). They support the contested governance claims.
- Reports from the Housing and Land Rights Network and the Internet Freedom Foundation. They support the displacement and surveillance concerns.

Verbatim quotes: none available.

## Drill-down
Breakdown layers: city (100), state, sector (mobility, water, ICCC, public space), funding source, and year.

```prism-calls
[
{"id":"f1","question":"How many papers on India smart cities per year, 2015-2026?","feature":"research.statistics","args":{"term":"India smart cities mission","group_by":"year"}},
{"id":"f2","question":"Which papers criticise the SPV governance model?","feature":"research.counter_evidence","args":{"term":"smart city SPV India governance"}},
{"id":"f3","question":"How has news coverage of the Smart Cities Mission trended?","feature":"news.trends","args":{"term":"Smart Cities Mission","from":"2015-06-01","to":"2026-10-23"}},
{"id":"f4","question":"Which states dominate coverage?","feature":"news.geography","args":{"term":"Smart Cities Mission"}},
{"id":"f5","question":"What is the sentiment on surveillance and ICCCs?","feature":"news.sentiment","args":{"term":"smart city command centre surveillance India"}},
{"id":"f6","question":"What does the evidence say about outcomes in ABD zones?","feature":"research.evidence","args":{"term":"area-based development smart city India outcomes"}},
{"id":"f7","question":"What are the post-2025 successor plans and their likely paths?","feature":"analysis.scenarios","args":{"term":"India urban missions after Smart Cities Mission"}}
]
```

## Exports

year,completed_share_pct

2020,30
2021,45
2022,60
2023,75
2024,85
2025,92
```

```

## Method and limits
- Windows: the SCM ran from 2015-06 to 2025-03-31. That is about 19 months before today (2026-10-23), and post-mission developments are not covered.
- Lanes and corpora: none queried, so no volumes, match mode or censoring can be reported.
- Coverage: partial, from memory, with a knowledge cutoff in June 2026.
- The counts are approximate ministry-reported outputs, not audited. They are not outcome measures.
- Interpretation: my reading that outcomes are thin and contested is a judgement, not a measured finding.
- Cannot answer: the share of contested claims, the news trend series, the corpus volumes, per-city performance.

## References
No references were retrieved. All figures are estimates from memory (est.). Candidate sources to verify them are listed under Evidence, and they have no [rN] identifiers because I did not confirm any specific citation.

## Verdict
- Answer: Smart cities in India is a heavily covered news topic (221 of 251 subject-lane articles are India-tagged [c1]). The research base is rising but thin on review-grade evidence, and the Prism corpus contains no review or guideline-tier paper on it [c1].
- Decision: Use this as a scoping brief to choose where to dig deeper (governance, SPV model, outcomes). Do not use it as proof of mission outcomes or impact.
- Confidence: low - only 7 papers carry readable abstracts and none is review-tier [c1]. Outcome numbers (spend, projects completed) are absent from the data.
- What would change it: Retrieving evaluation reports or audit documents with outcome data, or a review-tier paper.

## What the data shows
Volumes by corpus (subject lane) [c1]:
- Typed research papers: 323, window 2017-2025.
- Papers with a real abstract, title-anchored: 7, window 1990-2025.
- the health literature index records: 1, window 1990-2025.
- News articles: 251, window 2019-01-01..2026-06-01.
- Patents: 0 (2005-2024). Arxiv preprints: 0 (2005-2025).

Established: nothing. The note says no review or guideline-tier paper matched in the reading corpus [c1].

Contested: of 323 papers, 144 supporting, 108 qualifying, 5 contradicting, 66 neutral; contested share 35.0% [c1]. Reading: mostly positive framing with a substantial cautionary minority [c1].

Key numbers returned are technical, not policy outcomes. They all come from one 2025 chapter on HCI and VR in smart cities, with no India-specific population or period: 95% encryption efficiency, 92% gesture-recognition accuracy, 15 ms delay [c1]. I treat these as weak, single-source and not about Indian city outcomes.

Mission-term news (query "smart cities mission", mention match, 2024-06 to 2026-05): 681 articles, of which 498 are critical (73.1%, computed from [c2]).

## Trend
Research output rose from 24 papers in 2017 to 75 in 2025 (peak), a CAGR of 15.3%. The late third holds 173 papers against 69 in the early third (2.51x) [c1].

News on the broad subject fell: 84 articles in the early third against 53 in the late third (0.63x). The peak was 7 in a single month, January 2020 [c1]. Mission-term news since mid-2024 is flat: early third 209, late third 216 (1.03x), peak 47 in March 2025 [c2]. The share labelled critical fell to 43.5% in May 2026 from 68.0% in June 2024 [c2].

## Method and limits

The research window ends in 2025 [c1]; the brief’s general news window ends 2026-06-01 [c1], while the trend call is monthly through 2026-05-01 with an exclusive 2026-06-01 cutoff [c2]. The latest data therefore trails today, 2026-10-23, by 144 days (about 4.7 months) [c2]. News ingest lag is explicitly noted; the newest month is censored, so it is excluded from the trend series [c2].

Lanes are subject-matched Prism research, readable papers, the health literature index, news mentions, title-matching patents, and preprints [c1]. News trend matching is “mention” mode [c2]. Coverage checks passed index partition reads and historical row floors, which do not prove complete ingestion [c1][c2]. Counts are indexed records and classifications, not unique projects, expenditures, outcomes, or representative public sentiment. “Mostly positive framing” and the 35.0% contested share are Prism’s interpretation/classification [c1].
